headline: Microsoft surges 2.3% on a $600 price target from Morningstar while oil spikes nearly 6% — a big night for energy holdings.

portfolio.summary: A mixed session across the portfolio. Microsoft was the standout mover last night, jumping over 2% after Morningstar put a $600 fair value on the stock. CBA had a rough day on the ASX, slipping just over 1% amid a wobbly banking sector. The emerging markets ETF (VGE) quietly had a solid session, up 1%. GOOGL gave back about 1% with no clear news catalyst. Oil's near-6% spike is the big story for FUEL.AX holders — it closed up 0.7% today but watch for more upside.

movers.name: Microsoft
movers.note: Strong night last session — Morningstar published a report arguing MSFT is worth $600, well above its current ~$460 price. That kind of institutional endorsement tends to attract buying interest.

movers.name: Crude Oil (WTI)
movers.note: Oil jumped nearly 6% last night to $92.47/barrel. That's a big move and a tailwind for your FUEL.AX energy ETF.

movers.name: Alphabet (Google)
movers.note: Gave back about 1% last session with no specific news driving the dip. Likely some general rotation out of big tech on a day when Microsoft grabbed the spotlight.

movers.name: Commonwealth Bank
movers.note: Slipped $1.72 to $163.30 in today's ASX session amid mixed sentiment across the banking sector. No major CBA-specific news — broader sector caution appears to be the culprit.

movers.name: Vanguard Emerging Markets ETF
movers.note: A quiet but solid session today, up about 1% to $92.99. Emerging markets getting a lift as the AUD held steady and global risk appetite stayed reasonable.

movers.name: Take-Two Interactive
movers.note: Up 1.26% last session. GTA 6 hype continues to simmer — Take-Two's CEO was out publicly saying even former Rockstar employees find GTA's success hard to replicate, reinforcing the franchise's unique position ahead of launch.

markets.summary: Last night's US session was quietly positive. The S&P 500 and NASDAQ both ticked higher, with the NASDAQ up 0.42% — solid but not dramatic. The big story was crude oil surging nearly 6%, which rippled through energy stocks. Gold slipped 1% to $4,515/oz as investors rotated slightly away from safe havens. The Aussie dollar was basically flat at 71.7 US cents. ASX 200 data wasn't available for today's close.

indicators.name: S&P 500
indicators.note: Mild gains last night — market holding up well near all-time highs.

indicators.name: NASDAQ Composite
indicators.note: Tech-heavy index edged higher last night, led by Microsoft.

indicators.name: Crude Oil (WTI)
indicators.note: Nearly 6% spike last night — a major move. Good news for energy holdings like FUEL.AX.

indicators.name: Gold
indicators.note: Pulled back 1% last night as investors shifted toward risk assets.

indicators.name: AUD/USD
indicators.note: Flat — the Aussie dollar barely moved, sitting just above 71.6 US cents.

politics.summary: No Australian political stories came through in today's feeds. Could be a quiet Monday on the political front, or a data gap — either way, nothing to report today.

ai.summary: Today's AI news cycle was dominated by policy and regulation — governments and researchers are trying to map out the fast-growing patchwork of AI rules across health care, geopolitics, and US Congress. Not a lot of 'wow new feature' news today, but the regulatory picture is increasingly important for big AI companies like Google and Microsoft.

stories.title: National index tracks AI health care regulations as policy patchwork grows
stories.why_it_matters: A new national index has been launched to track the growing web of AI regulations specifically in health care. The US currently has no single federal AI law — instead, rules are being made state by state and agency by agency. For investors in companies like Google and Microsoft (both deep in health AI), this regulatory patchwork creates both risk and opportunity: whoever navigates compliance best gets a competitive edge.

stories.title: The geopolitical gains of EU Artificial Intelligence regulation
stories.why_it_matters: Analysis out today argues that the EU's strict AI Act isn't just about consumer protection — it's a geopolitical play. By setting the global standard for AI rules (similar to how the EU did with privacy via GDPR), Europe could force US and Chinese tech giants to comply with its framework or lose access to the EU market. That's meaningful for GOOGL and MSFT, which do significant business in Europe.

stories.title: A new project aims to map the AI policy ecosystem
stories.why_it_matters: Researchers are building a comprehensive map of the AI policy landscape — tracking who's regulating what, where, and how fast. The takeaway: AI governance is fragmenting globally, making it harder for tech companies to operate consistently across borders. For investors, this adds a compliance cost layer to big AI players like Google and Microsoft that's easy to underestimate.

stories.title: Cancel your Claude sub and get lifetime access to ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, and more for $60
stories.why_it_matters: A third-party deal is offering lifetime access to bundled AI tools — ChatGPT, Gemini (Google), Claude and others — for a one-off $60 payment. It's a sign of how commoditised AI subscriptions are becoming, which could pressure the recurring revenue models that companies like Google and Microsoft are building around AI. Worth watching as a trend rather than a crisis.

sport.summary: Round 13 wrapped up over the weekend with some cracking results — the Panthers won a classic, the Raiders got up, and the Dragons broke a drought. Round 14 kicks off Thursday night. AFL Round 12 coaches' votes are in, with Nick Daicos still leading the Brownlow count. Perth Bears news continues to trickle out ahead of their 2027 NRL debut.

stories.title: Panthers win a classic, Raiders salute, Dragons break drought — Round 13 wrap
stories.why_it_matters: Three big results from Round 13: the Panthers won a high-quality game that'll have fans talking, the Raiders picked up a win to keep their season alive, and the Dragons snapped what had been a lengthy losing streak. Round 14 starts Thursday night with Sea Eagles vs Rabbitohs at 4 Pines Park (7:50 PM). Broncos host the Titans at Suncorp on Saturday night — the Queensland derby to watch.

stories.title: Broncos 'BS' exposed in Madge nightmare; NSW Origin bolter's stunning statement
stories.why_it_matters: Fox Sports is calling out the Broncos after what's being described as a nightmare result under coach Michael Maguire. There's also an unexpected name reportedly pushing for a NSW State of Origin spot — described as a 'stunning statement' performance. No specific player named in the available data, but it's worth keeping an eye on as Origin selection looms.

stories.title: Every Perth Bears signing so far, best 17 for 2027 NRL season
stories.why_it_matters: The Perth Bears are building their squad ahead of entering the NRL in 2027. CODE Sports has compiled every signing made so far and put together a projected best 17. It's early days but the Bears are actively recruiting — a pathways (development) signing was also confirmed today, giving a young player a Top 30 squad deal. The new team is shaping up as a genuine expansion story to follow.

stories.title: Coaches' votes R12: Swans star among five perfect 10s, Daicos stays top
stories.why_it_matters: Round 12 coaches' votes are in for the AFL Brownlow Medal tracker. Nick Daicos (Collingwood) remains the leader. A Sydney Swans player was one of five players to receive a perfect 10 votes from coaches in Round 12 — a standout performance that boosts their Brownlow credentials heading into the business end of the season.

stories.title: 'What's the point?' Pies' brutal gauntlet explained — and why it could spark ruthless purge
stories.why_it_matters: Collingwood is facing a seriously tough run of games coming up, and Fox Sports is asking whether this brutal fixture could force the club's hand on player list decisions — potentially triggering a ruthless culling of underperformers. With Daicos leading the Brownlow and the Pies under pressure, this is a club at a crossroads mid-season.

watch_today.title: MSFT: Morningstar says it's worth $600 — still a hold, but a comfortable one
watch_today.detail: Morningstar published a report today arguing Microsoft is fairly valued at $600, about 30% above last night's close of $460. That's a big gap, and it's the kind of research that tends to attract institutional buyers over time. No need to chase it today, but this reinforces holding confidently.

watch_today.title: Oil spiked 5.85% last night — watch FUEL.AX for follow-through
watch_today.detail: Crude oil jumped from $87 to $92.47 per barrel overnight — a nearly 6% move. FUEL.AX (your global energy ETF) only moved 0.71% today on the ASX, so it may not have fully priced in that oil move yet. US energy stocks could push it higher when they trade tonight.

watch_today.title: CBA slipped 1% today — no panic, but worth watching
watch_today.detail: CBA closed at $163.30, down $1.72 on the day. The move appears to be sector-wide caution rather than CBA-specific bad news. At these levels CBA is still trading at a significant premium to peers on a P/E (price-to-earnings) basis — meaning it's already pricing in a lot of good news. Not a sell signal, but not a screaming buy either.

watch_today.title: GTA 6 launch narrative building around TTWO
watch_today.detail: Take-Two's CEO was publicly out today saying GTA's success is almost impossible to replicate — even for former Rockstar staff. This kind of commentary ahead of GTA 6's expected launch is designed to set expectations and drum up hype. TTWO was up 1.26% last night. The stock's upside is heavily tied to GTA 6 delivering — stay across any launch date news.

watch_today.title: No Australian politics news today
watch_today.detail: The politics feed came up empty today — a quiet Monday in Canberra. Nothing to act on, but keep an eye on any RBA-related commentary this week as rate expectations continue to shape bank stocks like CBA.
